title: Design an auditable RSC data-exposure boundary
businessContext: Developers assume that anything computed in a Server Component cannot reach a browser.
problemStatement: Design the system for A regulated portal with internal account records and public client islands. Produce the component/data-flow diagram, request and mutation contracts, cache/trust boundaries, capacity assumptions, failure recovery and rollout gates. State which decisions change between Next.js 15 and 16 instead of using a framework API as a substitute for an architectural guarantee.
constraints: Prevent sensitive props and errors from crossing the boundary.
Provide reviewable DTO contracts and regression evidence.
candidateTasks: Draw components and annotate ownership of data, identity, caches and durable work.
Specify contracts/schema and quantify the capacity/freshness assumptions.
Walk through the failure scenario and design measurable acceptance tests.
Compare the reference decisions and answer the changed-requirement interview prompt.

systemDesignReqs.scale: A regulated portal with internal account records and public client islands
functional: Prevent sensitive props and errors from crossing the boundary.
Provide reviewable DTO contracts and regression evidence.
nonFunctional: State an explicit latency, freshness and recovery budget rather than inventing guarantees.
Keep actor/tenant isolation and failure ownership observable.
assumptions: A patched App Router deployment; platform-specific infrastructure support must be verified.
Next.js version and Cache Components configuration are explicit design inputs.

hints: Mark server data modules server-only and define explicit public/actor-scoped DTO projections near the data-access boundary.

A future database column can silently leak if a DTO spreads a record. Use allowlist construction and a sensitive-field regression fixture; never rely on the client ignoring fields or on collapsed UI hiding serialized content.
alternativeApproaches: TLS protects transport against intermediaries; the authorized browser is still the receiver. Encrypting or hiding framework payload syntax does not authorize delivering secrets to that receiver.
commonMistakes: Claiming a cache API provides transactions, durable delivery or cross-region consistency.
Omitting authorization, recovery budgets or evidence from an otherwise attractive component diagram.

verification: Insert sentinel secrets and inspect HTML, RSC, script chunks and action responses.
Test different actors against the same resource ID.
Fail a server read and verify production error redaction.
nextjsPractice.next15: Use patched Next.js 15 and the router family named by the file path. Await request APIs where the App Router contract requires it; validate behavior in a production build.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
